title: How Bad Would Outspending Its Cash Flow Be For Meta Stock?
detail:
How Bad Would Outspending Its Cash Flow Be For Meta Stock?

Meta Platforms (META) expects capital spending of $130 billion to $145 billion in 2026. The company raised the bottom of that range from $125 billion in July. Executives plan to secure as much capacity as possible across 2026 and 2027, though they have not yet provided a spending figure for 2027. They also noted that strong operating cash flow puts Meta in a position to fund the build. So how close is Meta to spending more than it brings in?

Meta Already Spends Most Of Its Operating Cash

Meta came close during the June quarter. Cash from operations reached $31.9 billion, and capital spending consumed almost all of it. This left free cash flow, the cash remaining after capital spending, at $1.75 billion, against $9.02 billion a year earlier.

Over a full year, Meta still retains leftover cash, though less than before. Free cash flow for the twelve months to June totaled $41.0 billion, down from $50.1 billion in the prior twelve-month period.

If you have held Meta Platforms for years, your biggest question may be taxes, not how this one scenario plays out. See how a tax-aware transition works.

How Big Would A Cash Shortfall Be For Meta?

A spending push to the top of the 2026 range would leave Meta about $15 billion short if its cash from operations holds steady. At the bottom of the range, there would be no gap. The top of the 2026 range is $145 billion, compared to $130 billion of cash from operations over the past twelve months. Still, Meta held $90.3 billion of cash and short-term investments at the end of June. That is enough to fill the gap.

Executives noted on the July 29 call that infrastructure planning remains highly dynamic. The business paying for the build is still growing. Family of Apps ad revenue reached $59.4 billion in the June quarter, up 27% from a year earlier. Management also expects 2026 operating income to come in above 2025's.

What Does Meta Have Against A Cash Shortfall?

Meta has been borrowing more. Total debt reached $112 billion at the end of June, against $49.6 billion a year earlier. Management said the company has been adding debt to bring down its cost of capital. Even so, Meta's debt equals 6.0% of its market value, compared to 20.2% for the S&P 500. Over the past twelve months, Meta's operating income was 42.9 times its interest expense.

Meta is also bringing in partners. The company announced a venture with BlackRock in July to develop a new 1 gigawatt data center in El Paso, Texas. Management described such partnerships as a complement to Meta's own building efforts.

CNBC host Jim Cramer backed Reddit (RDDT) and Rocket Lab (RKLB) but passed on SiTime (SITM) on Thursday's "Mad Money," favoring stocks that have fallen over those priced for growth while interest rates climb.

The picks span social media, rockets, refiners and chips, yet one thread links them. The Federal Reserve (Fed) raised rates in September, and Cramer leaned toward stocks that had already sold off.

Does a Sell-Off Make Reddit and Rocket Lab Worth Owning?

Cramer said he wants to buy Reddit after its slide this year. In contrast, one caller said investors punished lost, unprofitable Google traffic and ignored Reddit's earnings from direct users.

Reddit is down over 12% in the last 3 months. Image: Trading View

However, CEO Steve Huffman called Google search referrals choppy in July, even as revenue grew 61%.

On Rocket Lab, Cramer said the failure to launch hurt the stock less than he expected. On Wednesday, Rocket Lab delayed the debut of Neutron, its medium-lift rocket, to 2027, Bloomberg reported.

Meanwhile, Rocket Lab reported a record $2.36 billion backlog in the second quarter, up 137% year over year. However, it has yet to turn a profit, and Neutron anchors that plan.

Where Does Oil Risk Sit in Cramer's Energy Calls?

Cramer prefers Chevron to Exxon, unless taxes complicate a swap. He told a caller Enterprise Products Partners earns from natural gas liquids, such as ethane and propane, not oil.

Cramer called Valero (VLO) a binary bet on the crack spread, the gap between crude costs and refined fuel prices. He tied the spread to the Iran war.

On SiTime, which makes silicon timing chips, he drew the clearest line.

"It's expensive, and I'm not recommending expensive stocks in tech or out of tech."

Jim Cramer, host of CNBC's "Mad Money," CNBC

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PKVCyfO7618

If the Fed keeps hiking, the same valuation test could reach crypto. Grayscale's rate hike outlook argues that higher rates hit assets unevenly.

The Fed meets Oct. 27-28, and futures price about a 27% chance of another hike.

Quick Read

Retiring, paying off a mortgage, and closing two credit cards in the same year dropped one woman's score from 805 to 735, despite zero debt.

Closing two cards slashed her available credit from $42,000 to $9,000, spiking her utilization from 5% to 22% on the same monthly spending.

Request credit limit increases before your last day of work, keep all cards open with small autopay charges, and never close your oldest account.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

A 68-year-old woman does three responsible things in one year. She retires in March, pays off the last $38,000 of her mortgage in June, and then closes two of her three credit cards to simplify things. By the end of the year, her credit score has dropped from about 805 to 735.

PeopleImages.com - Yuri A / Shutterstock.com

She owes nothing and has never missed a payment, but scoring models still reward active, well-managed credit, and she just removed most of hers. This happens more than people might expect. One Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) thread titled "Paid off my house, and my credit score plummeted" filled up. People kept telling the same story. Equifax (NYSE:EFX) warns that closing a paid-off card "lowers your total available credit."

Three Good Decisions, Three Separate Score Hits

The reality is that this individual's credit mix took the first hit. The mortgage was her only installment account, meaning a loan with fixed monthly payments, and once it closed, her file showed only revolving credit like credit cards. Money.com notes that paying off a mortgage or auto loan can lower your score because "it reduces your credit mix."

Utilization did the most damage. Utilization is the share of your available credit you're using. Closing two cards cut her total limit from $42,000 to $9,000. She still charges about $2,000 a month, and that same spending rose from 5% of her available credit to 22%. Paying in full each month doesn't help here, because issuers usually report the statement balance before her payment posts.

Reddit Inc. (RDDT) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this company have returned -5.7%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +2.1% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Reddit Inc. falls in, has gained 4.5%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Reddit Inc. is expected to post earnings of $1.30 per share, indicating a change of +62.5% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1.2% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.27 points to a change of +101.2% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $6.94 indicates a change of +31.6% from what Reddit Inc. is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Reddit Inc..
